parsed.explanation: No trans-specific criminalisation, no facility/bathroom statute, no documented border friction, and foreign documents govern identity — no known traveller-facing exposure. Absence of legal gender recognition and of gender-identity hate-crime coverage are resident-facing gaps, which the rubric weights only lightly and which a visitor's home-issued passport does not touch; the only operational consequence is slightly thinner recourse if a trans visitor is assaulted. The violence record is unquantified (no denominators), so the violence axis is undocumented rather than alarming. Institutional climate is documented as LGB-tolerant (referendum, civil unions, an openly gay head of state) and the state is well-instrumented, so silence on trans-specific harm is a moderately positive signal. But neither trans-specific acceptance nor a working trans-specific remedy is documented, and bathroom, ward and custody practice are open questions. Sits below the 0.75 anchors, which show enforced remedies and documented acceptance.
